newsitem.title: CANADA: Multi-Corp to sell telecom business.
newsitem.headline: Multi-Corp to sell telecom business.

text.p: Multi-Corp Inc said on Friday it agreed in principle to sell its telecommunications business to a privately held Florida-based telecommunications firm for at least US$30 million.
The unidentified purchaser will buy the business on the earlier of June 30, 1997, or within 30 days of the purchaser completing an initial public offering of securities.
Multi-Corp said the purchase price would be twice annualized gross revenues for the three months preceding the closing date. But the purchase price should not be less than US$30 million.
The purchaser will pay Multi-Corp a non-refundable deposit of US$2.5 million. If the purchaser fails to complete the deal, Multi-Corp keeps the deposit.

Up to the closing date, Multi-Corp said it would retain the right to sell up to 30 percent of the telecommunications business to any person. If that occurred, proceeds would be used to reduce the purchaser's acquisition price.
The deal is subject to certain conditions, including regulatory and board approvals and the completion of a sale agreeement.
Multi-Corp said its board determined that the telecommunications aspect of its business no longer fit with the long-term strategic direction of the company, Asian language enabling technologies.
